correctness.rationale: For each radius the defect M_r−Re(a r w+b r^2 w^2+c r^3 w^3) is a nonnegative trig polynomial of degree 3. Three distinct angular zeros must each be double, forcing a squared monic cubic with three unit roots. Its constant/sign and Fourier coefficients force B=−2Cr s and A=Cr²(s²+2 conjugate(s)); eliminating s gives d=B²/(4C)−A=r conjugate(B), so B nonzero and candidate r=d/conjugate(B)>0 is unique. Conversely these equations give the exact nonnegative Laurent square C r³|w³−s w²+conjugate(s)w−1|²/2. The self-inversive cubic discriminant Delta=|s|⁴+18|s|²−8Re(s³)−27 is negative iff all three zeros distinct unimodular; zero and positive discriminants yield the claimed boundary/nonexceptional cases. Sympy independently reconstructed Laurent identity, discriminant and the sharp exp(8z−4z²+z³) example. Degree≤2 has at most two distinct angular minima by the double-zero count, completing cubic minimality.
